48_marg3304: In the title the prophet’s lineage and time are noted. Among the names of his fathers is set Chusi, which is interpreted “my Ethiopian”; in which it is noted that he who was once an Ethiopian has turned to penance. As it is said: “Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands to God.” And rightly Sophonias, as the son of an Ethiopian, writes in what follows of the Ethiopians’ penance, saying: “From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia” they shall bring me offerings. In the days of Josias: just as those whom Elias enlightened are called the days of Elias, so those who lifted themselves up to God are the days of Josias, for Josias means “the lifting up of the Lord”, and he was a just man. And note at the same time that here no kings of Israel are set down, but only the kings of Juda, because the ten tribes had already been taken captive by the Assyrians under Ezechias.
48_marg3305: He prophesies the overthrow of Jerusalem and the captivity of Juda and Benjamin by Nabuchodonosor; a captivity seen to begin once Josias was slain, for his sons and grandsons are not to be thought to have reigned so much as to have been made a mockery by the Egyptian king and the Chaldeans, and tormented by various misfortunes. And since this captivity hung over the people for their crimes, lest the people say they were driven to idolatry by wicked kings, a just king was given them; and because the people persevered in the worship of idols while he was zealous with the zeal of the Lord, the Lord sets forth the just cause of his anger.

48_marg3344: Allegorically. But because their generation is in darkness, and they are sons of Lot, that is, turning aside from God, and born of incestuous unions, therefore, insulting the sons of Juda, that is, the true confessors, over their possession, they long to magnify their own borders. 48_marg3356: Woe to the provoking. The word is directed against Jerusalem, once a dove, afterwards ever sinning, and handed over to captivities, and again redeemed by the Lord.
48_marg3357: Allegorically. The Church is a city redeemed by the blood of Christ, and a dove for its simplicity and the multitude of believers. It is threatened because it has behaved wantonly towards God, and would not hear God’s law nor receive discipline, nor has it trusted in the Lord, because it would not draw near to him by working well, while it believes it can serve God and the world. Its princes, while they rage against those under them, are to be called lions rather than shepherds. Its judges too are like wolves that kill, ever abiding in the evening of darkness and not looking towards the rising of the sun; as if in the night, with no one seeing, they plunder the Church’s possessions, so that the poor have nothing to eat in the morning of the true light, since not even a little food was left for the needy. Its prophets too, that is, the teachers who ought to teach others from the scriptures, are senseless in faith, and as it were faithless, since by their deeds they destroy the faith they build up. Its priests too, who distribute the Lord’s blood to the peoples, act impiously against Christ’s law, thinking that in the ministering of the eucharist the life of the priests need not be looked into, but only the solemn prayer; of whom it is said: The priest, whatever blemish he has, shall not approach to offer the oblation to God. And though these evils are in the Church, the Lord is merciful in that he does not depart from the Church, and just in that he renders to each according to his deserts: when the morning comes after the night of this world, he will give judgement in the light, and neither he nor his judgement will be hidden; and when he demands from each the money entrusted to him, he will not act unjustly, but will destroy the proud princes and pull them down from their seats; and the corners will be scattered, that is, the crooked thoughts in which the Pharisees pray, despising the corner stone; the ways too will be made desert, according to that: the way of the wicked shall perish; lest they walk in pride and depravity; and their cities, built for evil, will be destroyed, so that they may not have wicked inhabitants. All these things I have threatened, O Church, so that, receiving discipline, you may not perish altogether.

48_marg3360: Wherefore. The Jews say that at the coming of the Christ they await, when all nations are gathered and God’s fury poured out upon them, the earth is to be devoured by the fire of his jealousy; and that just as before the building of the tower all spoke one language, so, all being turned to the worship of the true God, all will speak Hebrew and the whole world will serve the Lord.
48_marg3361: Allegorically. Expect me, so that being ready you may say: My heart is ready, O God, and so on. These things can be read of the first coming, when, the demon trodden down and all error taken away, and the earthly works too destroyed, the apostles spoke in all tongues; when, after vices and sins, God was seen to rise again in us; when all nations too are gathered to the faith and are kindled by the fire of God through fear of God’s anger, by which fire all earthly works in them are devoured, and one tongue is restored to all, so that each, laying aside his error, may return to the ancient speech of the confession of God, that with one mouth they may call on God, confessing that the Lord Jesus is in the glory of God the Father, in whose name every knee should bow, of those in heaven, on earth and under the earth. These things can also be said of the second coming, when, after the vices of the present age, while the Church awaits the coming of the bridegroom, the nations will be gathered to judgement, and kings brought together to the place of punishments; and then God’s fury will be poured out, punishing all evils, where the mighty will suffer torments mightily, and he who has sinned less soon wins pardon. Whence he adds: For with the fire of my jealousy shall all the earth be devoured: because, when the nations are gathered to judgement and the kings to punishment, whatever is earthly and belongs to the works of the flesh will be consumed throughout the world, so that, in those to be saved, all the briars and thorns being burned up, each of them may return to the ancient speech of the confession of God, praising God for ever and ever, and serve him constantly in his temple with united zeal.

48_marg3362: When the chosen lip is restored, all the blackness of the soul and its foul colour, and the dragon’s poison with which we were stained, will be left behind; and leaving the rivers of Ethiopia, the masters of perverse teachings by whom we were once watered, the scattered of Israel will offer gifts to Christ. On the day when the light of Christ has risen it will be said to each: thou shalt not be ashamed for all thy doings, that is, the most wicked thoughts with which you worked against God; and the pride with which he was lifted up against God and against his holy mountain, that is, Christ, will be taken away. And in place of the proud a humble people will be left, which thinks nothing that displeases God. And note that at the consummation of the world all names of rank will be taken away, and one humble flock will remain under the meek shepherd. Then the remnant of Israel will not deny the Lord, nor speak lies, that is, foolish fables, and a deceitful tongue is not found in their mouth, since Christ, who is the truth, speaks for them; for they will feed in one flock, that is, they will lie down in the Church, and from there Nabuchodonosor, that is, the devil’s onslaught, will not frighten them.
